einzeiler: The Fantasy Footballers celebrate their 2000th episode with Week 7 matchups and a game…
kurzfassung: The hosts celebrate the 2000th episode of the podcast by looking back at classic audio quotes from the show's history. They also break down Week 7 matchups and injury situations, offering start and sit advice for fantasy lineups. Finally, Jason faces a hilarious punishment on the Wheel of Shame after losing the fantasy face-off.
stichpunkte: Celebration of the 2000th episode of the podcast and appreciation for the listener community.
Injury updates and news from around the league, including Cole Kmet's expected season-ending knee injury.
A trivia game where the hosts try to guess who said famous quotes from past episodes.
Detailed matchup breakdown and start/sit advice for the Denver Broncos against the Arizona Cardinals.
Preview of the high-scoring matchup between the Green Bay Packers and the Detroit Lions.
Analysis of the Los Angeles Rams facing the Las Vegas Raiders amid roster changes and injuries.
Sunday Night Football preview featuring the Kansas City Chiefs and the Seattle Seahawks.
Breakdown of the rivalry game between the Dallas Cowboys and the Philadelphia Eagles.
Jason wears a Mona Lisa costume as punishment on the Wheel of Shame after losing the fantasy face-off.
Reading heartfelt listener messages reflecting on years of listening to the show.

clips.hook: Expectations versus reality in building a fantasy football community
clips.text: The hosts reflect on their early expectations that supporters would only subscribe during the football season for rankings, only to discover that the community endured and engaged deeply throughout the entire year.

clips.hook: A hilarious realization about forgetting your own ridiculous quotes
clips.text: The hosts laugh about how many episodes have been recorded and how difficult it is to remember hilarious or absurd statements made years prior.

clips.hook: Shocking playoff statistics for teams starting with a two and four record
clips.text: A concrete statistic is highlighted showing that only a small percentage of NFL teams managing a two and four start ultimately make it to the postseason.

clips.hook: A humorous trade proposal to undo past roster mistakes
clips.text: The hosts playfully suggest that two NFL franchises should simply swap wide receivers to undo previous personnel decisions and fix their current offensive struggles.

clips.hook: Trapped inside a classic painting during a live broadcast
clips.text: Struggling to put on a specialized costume for a penalty, one of the hosts humorously compares himself to a ruined painting left out in the rain.
